records.title: Scenario 1, Task 1: Build a Meeting Room Booking System
records.summary: Built a working meeting room booking system that replaces the shared spreadsheet. You chose the defaults, so it is configured as: 4 rooms (Cedar 4, Birch 6, Maple 10, Oak 20), 08:00–18:00 in 30-minute slots, anyone books with their name (no login), single bookings only, max 4 hours, up to 60 days ahead, and only the booker or an admin can cancel. What it is: a single standard-library Python web app (app.py) with a browser UI at / and a JSON REST API under /api/..., storing data in a local SQLite file (bookings.db, created and seeded automatically on first run). No installs needed. How to use …
records.judge_notes: The delivered app.py is a complete, runnable standard-library web app with a browser UI (availability grid, click-to-book dialog, cancel buttons, My bookings panel) and a JSON REST API backed by SQLite, with overlap prevention via a transaction plus unique constraint and immediate slot release on cancel. README.md explains how to run and use it and documents the API and rules; test_app.py provides 18 tests. The team asked clarifying questions and used the user's chosen defaults. records.title: Scenario 1, Task 2: Add a Room Usage Dashboard
records.summary: Added a manager dashboard to the meeting room booking system. You approved the defaults, so it is: a new page at /dashboard (no login) with a date-range picker (default last 30 days) plus 7/30/90-day quick links, and a JSON endpoint /api/stats. It shows KPI cards (total bookings, hours reserved, cancellation rate, rooms used/unused), a per-room table with horizontal bars for bookings and hours reserved, utilisation % (hours ÷ 10 h per weekday) and an allocation suggestion (unused / underused <15% / well used / heavily used >60%), bar charts for bookings by day of week, per calendar date and b…
records.judge_notes: The dashboard itself is substantively implemented in app.py: /dashboard with date range, KPIs, per-room table with utilisation and allocation suggestions, SVG charts for weekday/date/hour, cancellation table and summary, plus /api/stats. However the delivered DASHBOARD.md and the lead's own final reply admit the test suite is not green (2 failures + 1 error), including the cancelled-slot re-booking bug that undermines the cancellation data model the dashboard depends on; the lead's claim of a table rebuild fix is contradicted by the shipped DASHBOARD.md and unverified. records.title: Scenario 2, Task 1: Produce a News Report
records.summary: Produced a news report on AI at HKUST for students and faculty, anchored on the most recent verifiable dated event: the HKUST–China Telecom Global Joint Laboratory on AI for Telecommunications, signed at the HKUST campus on 21 October 2026 by CTG EVP Chen Kai and HKUST Provost Prof. Guo Yike (also the lab's director), followed by the lab's first Scientific Advisory Committee meeting. The requester approved the default plan (practical emphasis on access, academic-integrity rules, data privacy, teaching/assessment impact; web article + social post + newsletter blurb). Two reporters gathered sou…
records.judge_notes: The team delivered a well-structured, multi-channel report on the 21 Oct 2026 HKUST–China Telecom Global joint lab, with clear 'what happened / why it matters' framing and practical guidance for students and faculty. However, the anchor event is not the most recent verifiable AI event (the 18 Nov 2026 KAUST marine-intelligence centre is later and is cited in the same report), and the fact-checker's own follow-up noted the source 1 URL still appears truncated, so the copy is not fully clean for publication.

records.title: Scenario 2, Task 2: Fact-Check AI-Writing Detectors
records.summary: Wrote the fact-check article ai_detector_factcheck.md (about 2,300 words of body text plus a source list) for students and faculty on the claim "AI-writing detectors can reliably determine whether a university student's assignment was written by AI". Verdict: NOT SUPPORTED for the strong version of the claim (a detector verdict on one student's assignment being reliable enough to act on), while noting the weak version (better than chance on average on clean, unedited AI text) is partly supported. The article sets out the interpretation it tested, the evidence for detectors, four lines of evid…
records.judge_notes: The delivered article is a complete, well-sourced fact-check with a clear verdict, evidence, uncertainty section and audience-specific advice; the team also consulted the requester on interpretation and angle, who approved the defaults. Weaknesses: the body runs ~2,300 words against the editor's ~1,600-word target, several fact-checker items were left unapplied, and some figures (OpenAI 26%/9%, HKUST CEI quote, TextPulse) remain unverified — though these are explicitly labelled as such in the document, so the core request is met.

records.title: Scenario 3, Task 1: Develop a Simulated Investment Proposal
records.summary: 已交付模拟美股投资建议书：US_Stock_Investment_Proposal_HKD1m.md（约16KB）。 做了什么：先按您的要求询问投资目标/期限/风险偏好（您选择“使用默认值”：长期增长、10年以上、高风险承受、无收入需求、10–20%防御仓位），据此并行完成三项研究（美股估值与利率环境；ETF费用/回报及香港投资者的30%股息预扣税与遗产税；历史回撤、恢复时间与汇率），写出建议书，并经风控与客户沟通两位同事三轮审阅、逐条修订。 核心方案（HKD 1,000,000 ≈ USD 127,470）：VOO 50%、QQQ 20%、VXUS 15%、BND 8%、SGOV 7%；分三批（40/30/30）约6个月内建仓，每年再平衡一次。 请特别注意两点：1) 按峰值到谷底估算，组合在2000–02/2008–09式熊市中可跌约45–50%（约剩HKD 50–55万），高于您默认的30–40%承受度——若不能接受，建议QQQ降至10%、SGOV升至17%；2) 香港居民持有美股ETF：股息被美国预扣30%（约每年0.48%），且美国遗产税免税额仅USD 60,000，您的组合已超出（超额约USD 67,000，潜在税负约USD 15,000–25,000），建议咨询税务顾问（如爱尔兰注册UCITS等替代方案）。 审阅状态（如实说明，未获最终确认的部分）：风控最后一轮确认其…

records.title: Scenario 3, Task 2: The Future of the Semiconductor Industry: An HTML Slide Presentation

records.judge_notes: The deck fully satisfies the format, audience, research, implications and risk requirements, and is a substantive 14-slide browser presentation. However, the team's own reviewers found unresolved problems: slide 2 still contains a self-contradiction ('earnings cycle, not a bubble' vs price +32%/estimates +73%), the Nvidia CEO-resignation claim remains single-sourced and stated as fact, and several figures are unsourced or overstated. The final revision was never re-reviewed, so accuracy/consistency is not fully met.
